changelog:
v6.9 — tests that pin contracts, not tuning; a test-cost signal; tiers need a named trigger.

Features: /todo now carries one rule for every project and tier, Pin contracts, not tuning: exact-value assertions only on contracts (money, the output a seeded RNG gives for a seed, wire and storage formats, public signatures, access decisions, ordering guarantees); thresholds, tuning numbers, content tables, copy, layout and config defaults are asserted as invariants and bounds. A story is deep only when a trigger from the table can be named; with no named trigger it is standard (this replaces "when in doubt, choose deep"). Mutation and oracle runs cover the files that carry the trigger, not the whole diff. Browser specs for layout and copy may be tagged @volatile: per-story gates skip them and the baseline, midpoint and final checkpoints run them. New helper test-cost.js reports test lines added per source line added for the working tree, a commit range, a date window or a whole directory of repos; /run-todo and /do run it every wave or story and print TEST_COST_FLAG above about 2:1 as a prompt for the reviewer, never a gate. /review:status --test-cost runs it for a project or a fleet. Reviewers label coverage-only findings TEST-GAP; on a standard story with no named trigger they are recorded as deferred instead of fixed (deep stories still fix every finding). qa-engineer lists non-contract exact values, balance-gated soak harnesses and coverage for its own sake under What NOT to Test. review:specialize can record a Fast-iterating product and its contract surfaces in the Risk Map.

Measured: across 18 repos the worst projects added 60-80% of their lines since September as tests (3-4 test lines per source line), while only 2-9% of added test lines were ever deleted: the cost was accumulation, not rewrites, and it was not specific to games.

Migration: none required. Existing tiers and TODOs keep working; a deep tier with no named trigger is now flagged by the planning review.

--- v6.8 ---
v6.8 — automatic memory capture, per-prompt recall and cross-machine sync of memory notes.

Features: a plain-markdown notes store beside the JSON memories (Claude's native auto-memory dir, or MEMORY_DIR). A UserPromptSubmit recall hook attaches up to three full memories per prompt, ranked by BM25 plus a local embedder when one is already running (keyword-only otherwise), never blocking, at most 6 KB, off with MEMORY_RECALL=off or MEMORY_PROFILE=minimal. Where recall delivers, the startup block shrinks to the importance 4+ core (MEMORY_STARTUP=titles restores the title list; Codex keeps titles). Opt-in capture (MEMORY_CAPTURE=on) stages quote-verified, secret-filtered candidates from finished sessions for promote or discard, through ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, MEMORY_CAPTURE_KEY_COMMAND, an OpenAI-compatible server, or no key at all with MEMORY_CAPTURE_PROVIDER=claude-cli (your own claude -p login; text-only, hook-free, recursion-guarded). memory-capture.js sync carries notes between machines through the tracked docs/.output/.memory/notes (three-way, conflicts reported, never deletes, secrets skipped; MEMORY_SYNC=on automates it), and memory:backup now also copies the notes dir.

Measured: recall defaults were tuned on 65 blind-judged real prompts against 320-memory stores (cosine floor 0.70, keyword hits need 3 terms and a corpus-scaled score, machine-generated prompts skipped); details and limits are in the Memory System reference.

Migration: none required. Existing JSON memories, the engine and its hooks are unchanged and are read as-is. Capture and sync stay off until enabled; set MEMORY_CAPTURE=on in .claude/settings.local.json env. Windows and Codex: the CLI and sync work on both; the recall and capture hooks are Claude-only.

v6.7 — fleet rollouts no longer stop on project config or stale update records.

Fixes: fleet sync ignores untracked project-owned config (.agents/intake, .agents/learning-intake, .claude/settings.local.json) when checking for local toolkit edits and keeps it out of delivery commits. The updater no longer reports a file as edited when its recorded hash is stale but its bytes equal a version the toolkit shipped earlier; genuine edits are still reported.

Migration: none.

--- v6.6 ---
v6.6 — release-sliced planning, one-pass reviews, and a pinned secret engine with git hooks.

Features: /todo tags every story core or later and deep or standard, lists predictable owner decisions up front and gates sourcing and licensing; /run-todo builds the core slice, stops at a ship gate with a short release packet, keeps one write-once record per wave and verifies UI headlessly. Reviews are one pass, then done: every finding fixed or recorded with a reason, each fix proven by a test, the gate green. Secret scanning runs on the pinned, hash-verified Betterleaks engine, and managed git hooks scan raw commits, merges, am and pushes. feedback-digest takes --since/--until. learning-intake is renamed intake.

Fixes: generic secret rules no longer fire on code shapes, placeholders or bare PEM headers; binaries the engine refuses are scanned as text projections; staged files are read by blob id.

Migration: run node .claude/core/secret-engine-install.js once per machine (commits and Write/Edit fail closed without the engine). Updates install the git hooks into .git/hooks and retire the old learning-intake files; an adopter-owned intake command or skill is reported, not overwritten.
